title: RADIALLY DECOUPLED DUAL INDUCTIVE POSITION SENSING ARRANGEMENT
technical_field: The present disclosure relates generally to inductive position sensing arrangements, and more specifically to a radially decoupled dual inductive position sensing arrangement for use in vehicle pedal assemblies or other rotary devices.
background_art: A vehicle pedal assembly typically includes a pedal housing, a rotatable pedal, and a position sensor. When the position sensor is an inductive position sensor, it comprises an inductive sensor target rotatable with the pedal and a substrate positioned opposite the target. Existing vehicle pedal systems are disclosed in U.S. Pat. No. 11,614,765 and U.S. Patent Application 18/047,174.
summary_of_invention: The invention provides a pedal assembly for a vehicle with a pedal housing, a rotatable pedal, a rotary inductive sensor target, and a rotary inductive position sensing arrangement. The sensing arrangement includes a printed circuit board (PCB) with a first transmitter surrounding a portion of the PCB, and a second transmitter within that portion. First and second receivers are located between the transmitters. Rotation of the sensor target causes changes in the electrical voltages of the receivers, indicating the pedal's position. This arrangement can also be used in other applications like traction motors.

FIG. 3 is a bottom view of the inductive position sensing arrangement. FIG. 4 is a top view of the arrangement. FIG. 5 is a perspective view with a cut-away showing transmitters and receivers. FIG. 5A is a close-up of transmitters and receivers. FIG. 6 shows another example of the arrangement. FIG. 7 is a top view of a metal inductive sensor target. FIG. 8 is a block diagram of an electronic controller. FIG. 9 and 10 show alternative arrangements of transmitters and receivers.
detailed_description: The detailed description explains the components and operation of the radially decoupled dual inductive position sensing arrangement. It describes the pedal assembly (10) including a pedal housing (20), a pedal arm (30) with a sensor target (34), and the inductive position sensing arrangement (50) mounted on a printed circuit board (PCB). The PCB has transmitters (115, 120) and receivers (122-127) on its surfaces. The arrangement is designed such that rotation of the sensor target (34) relative to the transmitters and receivers induces changes in voltage within the receivers. These voltage changes are processed by an electronic controller (200) to determine the pedal's position and control vehicle functions. Specific examples of transmitter and receiver configurations, frequencies, and their placement are provided, along with an electronic controller block diagram. The description also covers alternative embodiments and operational aspects, including the use of different frequencies for the transmitters and the geometric isolation between them. Additional examples illustrate variations in transmitter and receiver layouts, and the potential application beyond pedal sensing, such as in traction motors.
claims: 1. 2. The pedal assembly of claim 1, wherein first transmitter includes a first transmitter coil having a circular shape that surrounds the first and second receivers and the second transmitter.

3. The pedal assembly of claim 2, wherein the second transmitter includes a second transmitter coil having a circular shape, the second transmitter coil being surrounded by the first transmitter coil.
4. The pedal assembly of claim 3, wherein the second transmitter coil includes a trace formed by etching.
5. The pedal assembly of claim 1, wherein the first transmitter transmits at a first frequency and the second transmitter transmits at a second frequency that is different from the first frequency.
6. The pedal assembly of claim 1, wherein the first receiver includes a plurality of turns provided in a symmetrical pattern surrounding the second transmitter.
7. The pedal assembly of claim 6, wherein the second receiver includes a plurality of turns provided in a symmetrical pattern surrounding the second transmitter.

11. The pedal assembly of claim 10, wherein the first sensor circuit provides an excitation current to the first transmitter and the second sensor circuit provides an excitation current to the second transmitter.

15. The inductive position sensing arrangement of claim 14, wherein the second transmitter coil includes a trace formed by etching.

16. The inductive position sensing arrangement of claim 12, wherein the first transmitter transmits at a first frequency and the second transmitter transmits at a second frequency that is different from the first frequency.
17. The inductive position sensing arrangement of claim 12, wherein the first receiver includes a plurality of turns provided in a symmetrical pattern surrounding the second transmitter.
18. The inductive position sensing arrangement of claim 17, wherein the second receiver includes a plurality of turns provided in a symmetrical pattern surrounding the second transmitter.

The inductive position sensing arrangement of claim 18, wherein the first receiver includes three first receiver coils and the second receiver includes three second receiver coils, and wherein the three first receiver coils and the three second receiver coils are interleaved, the inductive position sensing arrangement including a first sensor circuit having a first inductive position sensor interface to receive voltage signals from the three first receiver coils and output a first sensor angle value, and wherein an input/output interface of an electronic controller receives the first sensor angle value and the electronic controller is configured to control vehicle acceleration or deceleration.
20. The pedal assembly of claim 1, wherein the first transmitter and the second transmitter are a distance apart from each other to provide geometric isolation.
abstract: A pedal assembly for a vehicle that includes a pedal housing; a rotatable pedal; a rotary inductive sensor target rotatable in response to movement of the rotatable pedal; and a rotary inductive position sensing arrangement. The rotary inductive position sensing arrangement includes: a printed circuit board (PCB); a first transmitter provided on the PCB and having a shape that surrounds a first portion of the PCB; a second transmitter provided on the first portion of the PCB surrounded by the first transmitter; and first and second receivers provided on the PCB between the first transmitter and the second transmitter. A rotation of the sensor target induces a change in a first electrical voltage of the first receiver and a change in a second electrical voltage of the second receiver. The rotary inductive position sensing arrangement can be used as a position sensor in traction motors or in other non-pedal applications.
